$$53\,320-52\,800=520.$$
He would pay $\$520$ more.

classification.difficultyReason: Explain why a sequence of operations returns any permitted starting number.

inlines.text: Take a number that does not contain zero and in which all the digits are different.
Double the number and then add 4.
Cross out the zeroes in your answer.
What number do you get? Explain your answer.

answer.short:
The number you started with.

Before crossing out the zeroes, the result is 100 times the starting number.
answer.worked:
Let the starting number be $n$.

$$\begin{align*}(2n+4)\times5+12&=10n+20+12\\(2n+4)\times5+12&=10n+32\\(10n+32)\times10-320&=100n+320-320\\(10n+32)\times10-320&=100n\end{align*}$$

Multiplying by 100 appends two zeroes. Since the starting number contains no zeroes, crossing out the zeroes leaves the original number.

answer.short:

$$\begin{align*}69237\div3&=23079\\23079\div7&=3297\\3297\div11&=299\text{ remainder }8\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\text{Original remainder}&=8\times7\times3\\\text{Original remainder}&=168\end{align*}$$

entries.description:
We can also write a division as a fraction.
For example, 864 ÷ 8 = 108 can be written as:
\frac{864}{8}=108
Other examples using this notation are:
\frac{0}{3}=0 and \frac{108}{12}=9
When there is a remainder, we can write the answer using a mixed numeral:
\frac{27}{8}=3\frac{3}{8}
In the next chapter we will study calculations such as:
8×3\frac{3}{8}=27
